label: hot-path-avoidable-work
name: Per-call allocation, zeroing, sorting, repeated gathers, duplicated asserts or unconditional eviction added on a per-token, per-layer or spin path
description: What breaks: throughput. xfer_gofs runs about 4608 times per 4096-token prefill and adds a 128 KiB memset the loops overwrite, six heap vectors where the singleton sibling uses stack arrays, a std::sort emission order makes unnecessary, and a piece-major gather calling v_head_fn 32x more (3907183627); drain helpers construct and reserve a vector before the empty check inside a spin loop, and a TRON_ASSERT re-evaluates 8 std::function calls the caller already asserted (3907185740); ns_to_cycles paid on every entry before the `0 == wait_cycles` indefinite-wait branch (3350064944 'check for the else if (0 == wait_cycles) case first?'); free_staging_if_idle releases and rebuilds the same GOF buffers with no hysteresis (4674512577 'I'm always concerned with performance'). Procedure: identify functions on prefill/decode/spin paths (callers from token or layer loops); in added lines list heap containers, whole-buffer fills, sorts, nested gathers, asserts duplicating the caller's, and computations before a branch that does not need them; compare with the singleton sibling on the same path; for added frees on a counter reaching zero ask what steady-state pattern re-pays the rebuild. Since 2026-07 he sometimes has Claude word the perf concern and pastes it.
disposition_reason: No existing check reads for cost on a hot path; 4 rows over 3 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes for the static pattern scan and sibling comparison; sizing the cost needs call-frequency knowledge or a trace.

members.concern: xfer_gofs (the new batched GOF transfer function) runs about 4608 times per long prefill and does avoidable per-call work: a memset of up to 128 KiB the populate loops overwrite anyway, six heap vectors where the sibling single-GOF function uses stack arrays, a std::sort that order-of-emission makes unnecessary, and a piece-major V gather that calls v_head_fn 32x more than the path it replaces while widening a pre-existing cross-layer v_buf race.

detection.trigger: A new function on a per-token or per-layer path (called from prefill/decode loops) contains heap containers (std::vector), a whole-buffer memset/fill, a std::sort, or a nested loop that re-runs a gather per inner element, where a sibling function on the same path uses fixed arrays or does the gather once.
detection.procedure: Find the callers of the new function (grep its name in src/ and h/) and count calls per forward pass from the loop structure (layers x GOFs). Inside the function list every std::vector, memset/std::fill, std::sort and lambda call inside a loop. For each, read the sibling function that handled the singleton case (xfer_gof, gof::populate) and compare: fixed std::array bounded by a constant, zeroing limited to padded regions, order-by-construction instead of sort, gather once per (pos,head). For a shared scratch (v_buf) check what key it is indexed by versus the key of the busy flag (staging_busy) and name the race window.
detection.question: Does the hot-path function do per-call work (allocation, zeroing, sorting, repeated gathers) that its singleton sibling already avoids with bounded stack storage and emission order?

members.quote: xfer_gofs does some avoidable per-call work on the prefill critical path (a 4096-token 36-layer prefill runs this ~4608 times):
members.note: Wade computed 4096/128 tokens... x 36 layers = 4608 calls and ~576 MB dead stores (4608 x 128 KiB) - arithmetic from the hunk plus the constants. Also names the exact sibling helper (shuffle_v_entry_padded) and the 1024-vs-32 gather count. Secondary pattern in the same comment: shared-scratch-race-widened (v_buf keyed per gal/position but staging_busy keyed per gal/layer). Head 7f80aa17da evidence: gof.cpp:249-252 std::array<...,max_specs> bases/fetchers/qdatas/qlens, comment at :244-247 'without a sort or generic coalescing pass', std::fill only on padded regions (:294,:300,:323), no memset. So all three bullets were adopted.

members.concern: The decode drain helpers help_drain_gof and wait_for_coop_gof construct and reserve a std::vector before checking whether the queue is empty, adding a malloc/free per spin iteration per worker per layer per token where the old code allocated nothing; gof_rodeo_impl_batch repeats an assert fire_gof_rodeo already made (TRON_ASSERT is live in release, 8 std::function calls instead of 4); and the prompt-sized-pass predicate counts token jobs, so a decode pass with 32 or more sessions gets the escalated budget at the pre-barrier idle point.

detection.trigger: A diff replaces a zero-allocation loop (try_dequeue into a local) with a container that is allocated before the empty check, in a function called from a spin-wait or per-token path; or a diff adds a TRON_ASSERT that re-evaluates a callback already asserted by the caller on identical inputs; or a comment says 'generation keeps X' while the predicate tests a count that decode can also satisfy.
detection.procedure: grep the callers of help_drain_gof / wait_for_coop_gof (hw_q_released_layer spin, begin_attention_job) and state the call frequency. Compare the removed lines (gof_coop_task task; try_dequeue loop) with the added lines (std::vector constructed before try_dequeue). For the duplicated assert, follow fire_gof_rodeo into gof_rodeo_impl_batch and list the asserts on the same inputs; check whether TRON_ASSERT compiles into release builds. For the predicate, read the comment and compute which decode batch sizes make gof_jobs_span.size() >= hwkv_coalesce_tokens true.
detection.question: On the per-token spin path, does the new code allocate or re-assert where the old code did not, and does the budget predicate admit decode passes the comment says it excludes?

members.quote: the std::vector<gof_coop_task> is constructed and reserved before checking whether the coop queue has anything. These run from the hw_q_released_layer spin and begin_attention_job — per worker, per layer, per decode token
members.note: Three patterns in one comment: perf-avoidable-alloc-on-hot-path (primary), duplicate-assert-on-release-path (TRON_ASSERT stays in release, so cost is real), decode-budget-gated-on-token-count-not-pass-shape (also in 5498556672). He proposes the exact remedy: try-dequeue first, early-return on empty, fixed std::array bounded by max(4, coalesce_gofs). Head 7f80aa17da evidence: commit 'Replaced cooperative drain vectors with bounded std::array batches and immediate empty-queue exits in model.hpp'; hunk under 3960538961 shows std::array<gof_coop_task, drain_capacity> tasks; if (!try_dequeue(tasks[0])) return; and gof_prompt_sized_pass flag at model.hpp:1166; only one kv_complete_fn(layer) assert remains (model.hpp:3089).

members.concern: In monitor_and_wait (the mwaitx spin-wait helper) the new threshold computation calls ns_to_cycles on every entry, and Wade asks to test the `0 == wait_cycles` indefinite-wait case first so that callers who asked for an indefinite wait do not pay that cost.

detection.trigger: A hunk in a hot-path function (a wait, poll, enqueue or per-command routine) adds a computation (function call, division, static initializer) before a branch, and one branch of the following if/else chain does not need that computation.
detection.procedure: Read the whole function at HEAD. For each branch of the if/else chain after the added computation, check whether the branch uses the computed value. If a branch does not, and that branch is a common call pattern (grep callers for the special argument, here `wait_for_not_event(..., 0)` or timeout 0), propose reordering so the branch that does not need the value is tested first. Check whether the computation is `static const` (one-time init plus a guard check per call) versus per-call; state the actual per-call cost.
detection.question: Does a branch that runs without needing the newly added computation get evaluated only after that computation is paid?

members.quote: this is maybe a nit... but it seems like we should check for the `else if (0 == wait_cycles)` case first? This change is forcing a call to `ns_to_cycles` every time through here now, even if the caller asked for an indefinite wait.
members.note: Code fact at both 64ea13a671 and head b8739108f7 (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:112-124): `static const uint64_t mwaitx_min_cycles = ns_to_cycles(300) + 300;` then `if (wait_cycles > mwaitx_min_cycles) {...} else if (0 == wait_cycles) {...}`. Because the variable is `static const`, ns_to_cycles runs once per process, not every call; the per-call cost is the static-init guard check. Wade's 'every time' is an over-statement that nobody corrected. Author replied 'seems like a reasonable change'; Bill replied that ns_to_cycles could be made cheap and he would patch it. The branch order is unchanged at head b8739108f7, so the agreed change was not made in this PR.

members.concern: The staging-buffer free (free_staging_if_idle, which releases the GOF's two 8 KB host buffers whenever the in-flight DMA count reaches zero) is unconditional, so a workload that re-DMAs the same GOF repeatedly pays a full free + reallocate + repopulate (the 'swizzle', the data reordering into the hardware layout) each time with no hysteresis; he flags this as a possible performance regression to watch after merge.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a release/free of a reusable buffer or cache entry that fires on a counter reaching zero or on every completion event, with no delay, threshold, LRU or reuse check between the free and the next rebuild.
detection.procedure: Find the free function (grep for release_buffer, free_, evict, deallocate in the diff). Read its condition: is it only 'in-flight == 0'? Find every caller (grep the function name in src/ and h/) and the rebuild path (the function that reallocates and repopulates). Then list every production site that submits the same object again (grep the submit function: xfer_gof, backfill_shard, prepare_for_dma) and ask whether two submissions of the same object can occur close together (multi-shard fanout loops, speculation, retries). Estimate the rebuild cost from the repopulate function (does it copy and reorder the whole buffer?).
detection.question: Can the same object be freed and rebuilt repeatedly in steady state, and does the rebuild cost (copy + reorder) exceed the memory saved for that pattern?
